extracted.intended_audience: educators, historians, parents, and readers interested in historical etiquette and moral education
extracted.subtask_description: A historical set of numbered etiquette rules (Washington's 'Rules of Civility' with French Maxims) prescribing proper behaviour, manners, and social conduct for youth and company; includes original French phrases and English translations plus editorial commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1st. Every Action done in Company ought to be with Some Sign of Respect, to those that are Present.
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions done before others should be with some sign of respectful feeling to the entire company. (Includes citation: MAXIMES, CHAP. II French original.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle: public behaviour should visibly express respect for everyone present. No specific examples beyond the maxim; preserved original phrasing and historical context in adjacent commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2d. When in Company, put not your Hands to any Part of the Body not usually Discovered.
rubrics_metrics.description: In the presence of any one, never put your hand to any part of the person not usually uncovered. Practise this point of decency even with intimate friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance notes include French original. Emphasises forming a habit of modesty; hands and face are ordinarily visible and thus exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3d. Shew Nothing to your Friend that may affright him.
rubrics_metrics.description: Show nothing to your companion that may grieve or affright him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, direct injunction — avoid presenting disturbing or shocking things to others. No extended examples in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4th. In the Presence of Others sing not to yourself with a humming Noise, nor Drum, with your Fingers or Feet.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not seek amusement in singing to yourself (unless beyond hearing of others), nor drum with your hands or feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid distracting or self-entertaining noises in company; permissible only when alone/out of earshot.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5th. If you Cough, Sneeze, Sigh, or Yawn, do it not Loud, but Privately; and Speak not in your Yawning, but put your handkerchief or Hand before your face and turn aside.
rubrics_metrics.description: When you cough, sneeze, sigh or yawn, control the sound; do not make loud noises. If you must yawn, avoid speaking while yawning, press your mouth or turn aside and cover with handkerchief/hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes French original. Side-note (later French book): in sneezing do not 'shake the foundations of the house.' Emphasises discretion and minimizing disturbance to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6th. Sleep not when others Speak, Sit not when others stand, Speak not when you should hold your Peace, walk not when others Stop
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an incivility and impertinence to doze while company converses, to sit when others stand, to walk on when others pause, and to speak when you should be silent or listen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception for those in authority (e.g., a Master in class) who may walk alone at appropriate times. General rule: conform actions to the group's conduct and the situation's decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7th. Put not off your Cloths in the presence of Others, nor go out of your Chamber half Drest.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not dress or undress before others, leave your bed disarranged, or go out half-dressed (e.g., covered with nightcap). Take care with the state of your chamber/bed when going out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: French original emphasises seemliness in private appearance and leaving rooms properly; avoid exposing intimate dressing to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8th. At Play and at Fire its Good manners to give Place to the last Commer, and affect not to Speak Louder than ordenary.
rubrics_metrics.description: At play or at the fireside, it is impolite to make new-comers wait too long for places; also do not affect speaking louder than usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial note: Washington MS follows Hawkins in a mistranslation — the original also warns against becoming overheated or carried away by play. Guidance covers both giving up places courteously and avoiding excessive excitement/noisiness while playing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10th. When you Sit down, Keep your Feet firm and Even, without putting one on the other or Crossing them
rubrics_metrics.description: When seated, place feet firmly on the ground at equal distance and do not cross a leg or foot over the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes a composed, symmetrical seated posture; French original cited for 'order to be kept while seated.' (Note numbering skips 9 in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 11th. Shift not yourself in the Sight of others nor Gnaw your nails.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make continual shifting postures (stretching body, extending arms, adopting various postures) and never pare or gnaw your nails in public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls such actions 'insufferably impolite'; includes French originals condemning extending body/postures and nail-paring/biting in public.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12th. Shake not the head, Feet, or Legs rowl not the Eys, lift not one eyebrow higher than the other wry not the mouth, and bedew no mans face with your Spittle, by appr[oaching too nea]r [when] you Speak.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not shake your head, fidget legs, roll eyes, frown, or make faces; avoid spitting or letting saliva reach others while speaking — keep a reasonable distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises maintaining a reasonable conversational distance to avoid spraying spittle; enumerates facial and bodily gestures to avoid as impertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13th Kill no Vermin as Fleas, lice ticks &c in the Sight of Others, if you See any filth or thick Spittle put your foot Dexteriously upon it if it be upon the Cloths of your Companions, Put it off privately, and if it be upon your own Cloths return Thanks to him who puts it off
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not kill fleas or other disgusting insects in sight of others. If you see filth or phlegm on the ground, step on it; if it is on another's clothing remove it discreetly without showing it; if someone removes similar matter from your clothing, thank them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical anti-pattern guidance: do not call attention to another's filth; remove offensive things unobserved and express gratitude when aided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14th. Turn not your Back to others especially in Speaking, Jog not the Table or Desk on which Another reads or writes lean not upon any one.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not turn your back or shoulders to people when speaking to them; do not knock or shake a table/desk another uses; do not lean on or pluck at another's dress while conversing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes respectful orientation and avoidance of physical disturbance or dependence on others during conversation or when they are working.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15th. Keep your Nails clean and Short, also your Hands and Teeth Clean, yet without Shewing any great Concern for them
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain clean, short nails and clean hands and teeth, but do not display excessive attention or vanity about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hawkins gloss: 'without overmuch attendance thereon or curiosity.' Emphasises balance between cleanliness and modesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16th. Do not puff up the Cheeks, Loll not out the tongue rub the Hands, or beard, thrust out the lips, or bite them or keep the lips too open or too close.
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vulgar or uncouth facial gestures: do not puff cheeks, stick out the tongue, fiddle with beard or hands, thrust or bite lips, or keep lips excessively open or tight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates specific facial mannerisms considered 'vilainie' (vulgar); guidance is to preserve dignified facial comportment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17th. Be no Flatterer, neither Play with any that delights not to be Play'd Withal.
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not flatter people with honeyed words (which shows low esteem) and do not play practical jokes on those who dislike them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why flattery is contemptible (it assumes the other is easily duped); avoid joking at the expense of someone who finds it offensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18th. Read no Letters, Books, or Papers in Company but when there is a Necessity for the doing of it you must ask leave: come not near the Books or Writings of Another so as to read them unless desired or give your opinion of them unask'd also look not nigh when another is writing a Letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not read letters, books, or papers during ordinary conversation unless necessary and with permission; do not handle or peer at others' writings without consent, nor give unsolicited opinions; do not look over another's shoulder while they write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong injunction against intruding on others' private reading/writings and against offering unrequested critique; emphasises asking permission and respect for proprietorship of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19th. let your Countenance be pleasant but in Serious Matters Somewhat grave
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a pleasant, open and tranquil facial expression in general, but in serious matters exhibit an appropriate degree of gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: French original adds that the face should not be fantastic, changeable, or show signs of an unquiet mind; balance openness with situational seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20th The Gestures of the Body must be Suited to the discourse you are upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the gestures of your body be appropriate to the subject of your discourse; avoid excessive or awkward gesticulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hawkins note: gestures should agree with the matter of discourse (example: do not point to earth when speaking of heaven). The original warns against excessive and awkward gestures and advises elegant posture while speaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21st. Reproach none for the Infirmaties of Nature, nor Delight to Put them that have in mind thereof.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reproach or ridicule people for natural infirmities or derive pleasure from reminding them of such weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partially present in the chunk; guidance condemns taunting or making sport of others' natural disabilities or conditions. (Entry includes surrounding parenthetical from the text.)
